$comment: Conformance vectors for ADR-PACK-0001. These expectations are FROZEN. They are not regenerated: if a committed expectation stops matching, either the implementation is wrong or the law changed — and a change to the law is an ADR amendment, never a re-run of a generator. Where this file and ADR-PACK-0001 disagree, the ADR governs and this file is the defect.
acceptance_criterion: Two independent implementations receiving the same packs, in any input order, must either produce the same effective manifest by value identity and the same canonical hash, or produce the same typed refusal.

canonicalization.note: Reused verbatim from dsm_primitives. No new hashing law is introduced. An implementation that reproduces these hashes with its own canonicalizer has proven the canonicalizer too.

governs: ADR-PACK-0001 — Pack Composition, Precedence and Resolution Refusal
how_to_use: For each vector, assemble its pack documents from `packs` (a SET — the listed order is transport only).
Call resolve(packs, evaluated_at, resolver_version) and compare against `expected`.
Resolved: the effective manifest must match by VALUE IDENTITY and its canonical hash must equal effective_manifest_hash.
Refused: the phase, the COMPLETE refusal set and refusal_hash must all match. 'It failed' is not a pass.
Re-run every vector under every permutation of its input order. Any permutation-dependent output is a defect, not a variation.
A vector whose pack carries schema_valid=false must still be run: the resolver refuses it on its own, without relying on schema validation having happened.

fiduciaire.base@0.1.0.why: Domain layer. Introduces every governed path and fixes its control pair.

fiduciaire.base@0.2.0.why: Introduces required_checks.review_cycle_days and declares NO control for it.

jurisdiction.fr@0.1.0.why: Jurisdiction FR. Peer of MA; its contributions commute with MA's.

jurisdiction.fr@0.1.1.why: Peer contribution to a `replace` path — competes with jurisdiction.ma@0.1.1.

jurisdiction.fr@0.7.0.why: Peer of jurisdiction.ma@0.7.0, claiming the same new path with incompatible merge semantics at equal rank and equal specificity.

jurisdiction.ma@0.1.0#mirror-copy.why: Byte-different copy of jurisdiction.ma@0.1.0: only provenance.source_ref differs. content_hash must be identical (R12) — a referent is never its carrier.

jurisdiction.ma@0.1.1.why: Peer contribution to a `replace` path — competes with jurisdiction.fr@0.1.1.

derogations.justification: Statutory retention period for the jurisdiction exceeds the domain default.

jurisdiction.ma@0.2.0.why: Raises retention_years under a signed, scoped, expiring derogation.

jurisdiction.ma@0.3.0.why: Raises a `requires_derogation` path carrying no derogation at all.

derogations.justification: Statutory retention period for the jurisdiction exceeds the domain default.

jurisdiction.ma@0.4.0.why: Derogation whose window is empty (not_before >= expires_at). Schema-valid, law-invalid: exactly the class the schema cannot catch.

jurisdiction.ma@0.5.0.why: Attempts to relax an inherited `requires_derogation` back to `open`.

jurisdiction.ma@0.6.0.why: Attempts to re-declare merge semantics fixed by the introducing layer.

jurisdiction.ma@0.7.0.why: Flips an inherited merge AND opens a new path its peer also claims. Contributes the refusal whose `detail` sorts first but whose `path` sorts last.

jurisdiction.ma@0.8.0.why: Two unmet requirements. Both refusals share (code, path, pack_refs) and differ only in `detail`, so the primary key alone leaves them tied — only the total tie-break orders them. The requirements are listed in anti-canonical order so that an implementation falling back on 'the order I built them in' produces a different refusal_hash.

jurisdiction.ma@0.9.0.why: Requires a domain range the present domain pack does not satisfy.

organization.demo@1.0.0.why: Organization layer. Renames one label under an `open` control.

organization.demo@1.1.0.why: Highest layer attempts a `forbidden` path. Precedence is not sovereignty.

organization.demo@2.0.0.why: Overrides a leaf covered by no control declaration. Must fail closed (R3bis / D4).

regulator.ma@0.1.0.why: Invents a fifth layer. The chain is closed at four (R1); an unknown layer is a typed refusal, never a silent extra rank. Schema-INVALID by design: the enum already refuses it, and the resolver must refuse it too rather than rely on the schema.

vectors.why: The milestone: three fictional layers load, conflict, and resolve to one canonical manifest. vocabulary.labels.grand_livre is contested and the organization wins it — under a control the domain layer left `open`, never by rank alone.
Byte-identical to three-layer-baseline except for input order. Same manifest, same hash. The list is transport; the input is a set (R7).
The same pack supplied twice from two different carriers. It deduplicates by content, and the manifest is identical to three-layer-baseline: a referent is never its carrier (R12).
Two jurisdiction packs at equal rank. Their contributions are `union`, which commutes, so peers are permitted and the fold is order-free.
retention_years is raised 5 -> 10 under a derogation that names the path literally, cites an authority, and is in force at evaluated_at. resolution_rule is derogated_override.

Boundary case. No packs is not an error: it resolves to an empty manifest recording that NO rules were in force. A consumer must read that as 'nothing governed here', never as 'anything permitted' — the empty manifest authorizes nothing.
Two peers, `replace` semantics, different values, nothing to distinguish them. Refusing is the correct answer; picking a winner would require an order that does not exist (R4/R7).
`forbidden` is absolute and is checked BEFORE any derogation is consulted, so no authority and no rank reaches this path (R5).
The permission floor is requires_derogation and no derogation covers the path. Refusal, not a silent grant.
Identical packs to derogation-valid, different evaluated_at. Evaluation time is an input (R8): same rules, different instant, different lawful outcome.
Empty derogation window. Fails closed in P4 unconditionally — even though the path it names would have been contested anyway, the malformed derogation alone refuses the resolution.
override may be tightened, never loosened. A layer cannot vote itself more freedom than the layer that introduced the field granted it (R3).

detail.reason: merge semantics are fixed by the introducing layer

vectors.why: merge is fixed at introduction and is not overridable at any rank. Allowing a higher layer to flip union -> replace would change the MEANING of a field silently (R3).

A leaf covered by no control declaration takes {merge: replace, override: forbidden}. An undeclared field is not an open field. This mirrors verify_hash failing closed on an unknown prefix (R3bis/D4).
A fifth layer is refused in P1 rather than ranked. Note the pack is deliberately schema-invalid: the resolver must refuse it on its own, without leaning on the schema having run.

detail.reason: same pack_id at multiple versions in one resolution

vectors.why: The same pack_id at two versions in one resolution. Which version governs is undecidable, so it is refused rather than resolved by list position.
A pack's own declared requirement is unmet. Checked in P2, before any value is composed.

detail.reason: merge semantics are fixed by the introducing layer
competing merge semantics at equal specificity
merge semantics are fixed by the introducing layer

vectors.why: Two refusals sharing one code. R9 orders them by `path`; sorting the whole refusal object canonically would order them by `detail`, which comes first alphabetically and is prose. The two orders disagree here, so this vector separates the rule from a plausible imitation of it — and because the refusal set is hashed, the disagreement is a different refusal_hash, not a cosmetic difference.

Two refusals identical in (code, path, pack_refs). The primary key cannot separate them, so an implementation without the total tie-break falls back on construction order — here, the order the author happened to type the requirements in. That is exactly the input-order dependence R9 exists to remove, hiding one level down inside a hashed structure.
